extracted.intended_audience: immigration attorneys, petitioners/employers, DHS/USCIS/CBP adjudicators, and nonimmigrant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and adjudicative standards governing admission, extensions, maintenance, revocation, and special-class rules for nonimmigrant classifications (including employment classes and T nonimmigrant/victim of trafficking provisions). Includes filing procedures, evidentiary expectations, and confidentiality protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonimmigrant classification and subclassification designations
rubrics_metrics.description: For administering nonimmigrant provisions, specific administrative subclassifications and designation codes (A-1, B-1, H-1B, L-1, T-1, U-1, TN, etc.) are established and used to refer to appropriate nonimmigrant classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation enumerates the mapping between section 101(a)(15) statutory categories and CFR designations (e.g., 101(a)(15)(H)(i)(B) = H-1B). Use the listed designations when identifying classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every nonimmigrant applicant must establish admissibility to the United States or that any ground of inadmissibility has been waived under section 212(d)(3) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon application for admission the alien must present a valid passport and valid visa unless waived; passport generally must be valid for a minimum of six months from the expiration date of the contemplated stay (unless otherwise provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to depart
rubrics_metrics.description: At time of admission or extension, the nonimmigrant must agree to depart the United States at the expiration of the authorized period or upon abandonment of status and comply with applicable departure procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with departure requirements (including biometrics) may constitute failure to maintain nonimmigrant status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond requirement to ensure maintenance of status
rubrics_metrics.description: At time of application for admission or extension, an alien may be required to post a bond on Form I-352 in the sum of not less than $500 to ensure maintenance of status and departure if required by appropriate authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bond may be required by CBP Commissioner, USCIS Director, immigration judge, or BIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readmission / automatic revalidation conditions (specified classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspecting officers shall readmit certain nonimmigrants to complete unexpired periods of admission (e.g., under sections 101(a)(15)(F), (J), (M), (Q)(ii)) if specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions commonly include: admissibility; absence not exceeding 30 days to contiguous territory/adjacent islands; possession of a valid passport (unless exempt); presentation of Form I-94 and appropriate endorsed Forms (I-20, DS-2019), or Certification Letter for certain programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and evidence requirements for extension/amendment (employment classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants/petitioners seeking extension of or amendment to stay for many employment-based nonimmigrant classes must file Form I-129 with prescribed fee and initial evidence specified in §214.2 and form instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependents may be included on the petition only in limited circumstances (e.g., petition for only one worker when form version provides). Otherwise, dependents file Form I-539.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-539 for other nonimmigrant extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-employment nonimmigrants (and others not required to use I-129) must file Form I-539 with the required fee and initial evidence specified in §214.2; family group filings allowed where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-applicants in the same family group may be included; extensions for family members must be for same period; shortest period among family members dictates all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes ineligible for extension of stay
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain nonimmigrant classes are ineligible for extension of stay (e.g., B-1/B-2 admitted under Visa Waiver Pilot Program; C-1/C-2/C-3; D-1/D-2; K-1/K-2; certain duration-of-status admissions; certain S, Q, or Guam-CNMI program admissions beyond statutory limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation lists specific categories and circumstances of ineligibility; check the enumerated subparagraph for applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely filing and discretionary excusal of untimely extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension/amendment will not be approved if previously accorded status was not maintained or expired before filing, except USCIS may excuse late filing where delay was due to extraordinary circumstances beyond control and other conditions are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS may excuse late filing without separate application if: delay due to extraordinary circumstances; applicant/beneficiary hasn't otherwise violated status; remains bona fide nonimmigrant; not subject to deportation/removal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deference to prior USCIS determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: When adjudicating a Form I-129 request involving same parties and same facts, USCIS gives deference to its prior determination of eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deference will not be given if prior approval involved a material error, there has been material change in circumstances or eligibility requirements, or there is new material adverse information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of maintenance of status (types of evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting an extension/amendment on Form I-129, applicant/petitioner must submit supporting evidence establishing maintenance of previously accorded status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include copies of paystubs, W-2s, quarterly wage reports, tax returns, contracts, and work orders; list is illustrative but not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary nature of extension/amendment decisions and nonappealability
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may grant an extension or amendment in its discretion where eligibility is demonstrated; denial of an extension or amendment may not be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide evidence supporting both eligibility and favorable exercise of discretion when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of nonimmigrant status
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the period of initial admission or extension, nonimmigrant status may be terminated by revocation of a waiver, passage of a private bill conferring permanent resident status, or notification in the Federal Register on national security/diplomatic/public safety grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination may occur during admitted period; grounds include revocations or statutory/administrative actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary visitors (B-1/B-2) and transit aliens (C-class) may not engage in employment. Any other nonimmigrant may not engage in employment unless accorded classification authorizing employment or granted permission under the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonimmigrants may only engage in authorized employment; unauthorized employment constitutes failure to maintain status under section 241(a)(1)(C)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Full and truthful disclosure of all information requested by DHS is a condition of admission and continued stay; willful failure to provide truthful information (regardless of materiality) constitutes failure to maintain status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure accuracy and honesty in all DHS interactions and filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal-activity standard for termination of status
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonimmigrant's conviction in a U.S. jurisdiction for a crime of violence for which a sentence of more than one year may be imposed constitutes failure to maintain status under section 241(a)(1)(C)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The potential sentence (even if not imposed) is controlling for this failure-to-maintain-status finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education privacy reporting (FERPA waiver for F, J, M students)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS has determined that waiving FERPA for F and M students and J exchange visitors is necessary for implementation of 8 U.S.C. 1372; educational institutions may not refuse to report required information on FERPA grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver authorizes and requires reporting only to the extent 8 U.S.C. 1372 and §214.3(g) require it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health care occupation credentialing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens coming to the U.S. to perform labor in certain health care occupations must obtain a certificate from an approved credentialing organization or a certified statement (for nurses) and present it to DHS as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must conform to 8 CFR 212.15(d)/(h) and related paragraphs; evidence of prior licensure/employment before specified dates may establish waiver eligibility for TN workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension/change denial where health-care certification missing or late
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition/application to extend or change status for a health-care worker will be denied if the petitioner/applicant fails to submit required certification with the petition or submits certification more than 1 year after initial admission (subject to limited transitional relief).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited temporary admission/extension without certification may be permitted for up to 1 year, but subsequent eligibility requires timely certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial/bar on petitions due to Department of Labor debarment
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon DOL debarment under 20 CFR part 655, USCIS may deny petitions for certain nonimmigrant statuses filed by that petitioner for at least 1 year and up to 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length of bar is based on severity; USCIS will explain decision, time period, and reasons in a written notice to the petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of stay rules (validity periods and brief pre/post admission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain classifications (E-1, E-2, E-3, H-1B, L-1, TN, etc.) may be admitted for the petition validity period (or as otherwise authorized) plus up to 10 days before and after the validity period. Work is authorized only during the validity period unless otherwise authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 10-day pre/post period is for arrival and departure; work is not authorized unless specifically allowed under relevant regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for cessation of employment
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien admitted under certain employment-based classifications who stops the qualifying employment will not be considered to have failed to maintain status solely due to cessation of employment for up to 60 consecutive days or until the end of the authorized validity period, whichever is shorter, once during each authorized validity period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS may shorten or eliminate this 60-day period as a matter of discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class-specific modifications to general requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The general requirements in §214.1 are modified for specific nonimmigrant classes as described in §214.2 (Table 1 lists classes: visitors, students, intracompany transferees, temporary employees, religious workers, T and U visas, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the specific §214.2 subsections for tailored admission/extension/maintenance requirements and evidentiary standards for each class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for T-1 nonimmigrant status (victim of severe trafficking)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for T-1 status an applicant must meet statutory and regulatory criteria demonstrating they are a victim of a severe form of trafficking in persons and otherwise satisfy the elements required by section 101(a)(15)(T) of the Act and the subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS performs a bona fide determination, considering the totality of circumstances and the evidence submitted; see §214.202–§214.206 for elements and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide determination for T applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS must determine that the applicant is a bona fide victim of a severe form of trafficking using the evidence submitted and applicable definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determination is based on the totality of circumstances and may include concordant evidence such as declarations, police reports, affidavits, and corroborating documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical presence requirement for T status
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for T nonimmigrant status must demonstrate physical presence in the United States (or at a port of entry) as a result of having been a victim of trafficking, as required by statute and regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidentiary standards and biometric submission rules apply; see §214.204 and §214.207 for details and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with reasonable request for assistance in trafficking investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: A condition of T nonimmigrant status is compliance with any reasonable request to assist in detection, investigation, or prosecution of trafficking unless an exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS considers cooperation with law enforcement; failure to comply with a reasonable request (as notified by LEA) can be grounds for revocation of T status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extreme hardship involving unusual and severe harm (T-related relief)
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may consider extreme hardship involving unusual and severe harm to the applicant as a factor in discretionary decisions related to T status and derivative relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule references exceptional hardship standards; applicants should supply medical, police, or other credible evidence to support claims of extreme hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual numerical limit for T visas
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an annual numerical limit applicable to T visas as prescribed by statute/regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation describes the annual limit and how derivative approvals affect or do not affect the cap; consult §214.210 for numeric specifics and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and filing for eligible family members (derivatives) for T status
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules define which family members qualify as eligible derivatives (spouse, children, certain parents/siblings under conditions) and how they may accompany or follow to join the principal T-1 applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special provisions include protection for children born after filing, age‑out protections, marriage/stepfamily rules, and evidentiary and biometric submission requirements for derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age-out and new-child protections for T derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: A child born after filing the principal T-1 application is deemed an eligible family member; certain age-out protections apply for principals who were under 21 when filing (and related sibling/parental protections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed subrules specify dates/times (filing, adjudication, admission) that control eligibility; see the subsections addressing relationship and age-out protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence demonstrating present danger of retaliation for derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: To seek derivative T status on basis of present danger of retaliation, applicants must demonstrate the danger via documentation such as LEA statements, personal statements, court documents, police reports, news articles, affidavits, or previous advance parole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS may contact the LEA involved; any credible evidence is acceptable and may be from U.S. or foreign sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biometric submission and evidentiary standards for T and derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for T nonimmigrant status and derivatives must comply with biometric submission requirements and evidentiary standards set forth in §§214.204(b) and (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow form instructions and submit requested biometric and supporting documentation to establish eligibility and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of T nonimmigrant status — law enforcement need or exceptional circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may extend T-1 status beyond initial periods (beyond 4 years) in 1-year increments if an LEA certifies the applicant's continued presence is necessary for detection/investigation/prosecution or if USCIS finds exceptional circumstances warrant extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must file the designated form with evidence; evidence of law enforcement need includes LEA declarations or other credible evidence; exceptional circumstances may be supported by medical records, court records, correspondence, affidavits, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely filing for T extensions and discretionary untimely relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should file extension requests before T status expires; if status has expired, the applicant must explain the untimely filing and USCIS may exercise discretion to approve untimely filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a written explanation and supporting evidence showing reasons for delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of law enforcement need for T extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence demonstrating law enforcement need may include a new LEA declaration, letters from prosecutors/judges/officials on agency letterhead, emails/faxes from LEAs, or any other credible evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation submitted should specifically state why the applicant's presence is necessary to assist detection/investigation/prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional-circumstances evidence for T extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of exceptional circumstances to justify extension beyond statutory periods may include the applicant's statement, medical records, police/court records, news articles, consular correspondence, and affidavits from knowledgeable individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS evaluates exceptional circumstances in its discretion; submit corroborating documentation where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory extension of status for adjustment applicants (T)
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will automatically extend T status when a T nonimmigrant properly files an application for adjustment of status during their period of T status in accordance with 8 CFR 245.23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No separate application or supporting evidence for the extension is required when adjustment application is properly filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic and discretionary revocation of T approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved derivative T application is automatically revoked if the family member notifies USCIS they will not apply for admission; USCIS may revoke approved T status after notice if approval violated statutory/ regulatory requirements, or other grounds such as divorce (for T-2) or LEA withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation follows notice-of-intent procedures with opportunity to rebut; automatic revocations cannot be appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation procedures and opportunity to rebut
rubrics_metrics.description: Before revoking an approved T application USCIS issues a written notice of intent to revoke stating grounds and time for rebuttal (30 days); USCIS will consider all relevant evidence and may notify LEA, consular offices, or ORR of revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should timely submit rebuttal evidence within 30 days; appeal rights may apply per 8 CFR 103.3 for some revocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of revocation on principal and derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocation of T-1 status terminates the principal's status and automatically terminates derivative T status; pending derivative applications will be denied; any waivers of inadmissibility granted with the application are revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation does not affect the annual numerical limit in §214.210.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal proceedings and enforcement discretion for T applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS may institute removal proceedings for conduct committed after admission or for undisclosed conduct or misrepresentations; ICE will maintain policy regarding exercise of discretion and enforcement involving T visa applicants and nonimmigrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with credible victim claims may still face removal proceedings for other conduct; ICE/USCIS will consider victimization and policy in discretionary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS employee referral obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS employees who encounter noncitizens believed to be trafficking victims and not already working with an LEA may consult with ICE victim protection/investigation officials and may refer victims to appropriate LEAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a credible claim of victimization exists, USCIS may advise the individual to submit a T application and seek protections, provided this advice does not compromise safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and restrictions on disclosure of T-related information
rubrics_metrics.description: Use or disclosure of information related to pending or approved T applications is prohibited except to certain DHS/DOJ/State employees for legitimate purposes or under exceptions in 8 U.S.C. 1367(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information protected under 8 U.S.C.1367(a)(2) may be disclosed to federal prosecutors to meet constitutional obligations; agencies receiving information are bound by confidentiality provisions. DHS officials may not make adverse admissibility determinations based solely on information from the trafficker except where the applicant was convicted of certain crimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization for derivative T nonimmigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: A derivative granted T nonimmigrant status may apply for employment authorization by filing an Application for Employment Authorization; for derivatives in the U.S. the EAD may be filed concurrently with the derivative T application, while for derivatives abroad, EAD filings occur after admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved, the derivative receives employment authorization pursuant to 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(25) for the remaining period of derivative status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel abroad and reentry rules for derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: To return to the U.S. and continue derivative T status after travel abroad, the derivative must have advance parole (section 212(d)(5)) or obtain a T nonimmigrant visa (unless visa exempt) and be admitted as a T nonimmigrant at a designated port of entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan travel carefully; obtaining appropriate travel documentation prior to departure prevents inadmissibility upon return.
